texts: Francisco Rolão Preto was a Portuguese politician and journalist. He was a key figure in the National Syndicalist movement in Portugal during the 1930s. Rolão Preto was the founder and leader of the National Syndicalist movement, which was a fascist movement that sought to establish a corporatist state in Portugal. He was influenced by the ideas of Italian fascism and sought to create a similar movement in Portugal. However, his movement was eventually banned by the authoritarian Estado Novo regime of António de Oliveira Salazar, and Rolão Preto was forced into exile.

Francisco Rolão Preto was a prominent Portuguese political figure and intellectual who founded the National Syndicalist Movement in 1932. He was one of the leading advocates of fascist ideology in Portugal during the early 20th century, drawing inspiration from Italian Fascism and integrating it with traditional Portuguese values. Initially supportive of António Salazar's Estado Novo regime, he later became one of its most vocal critics when he felt it deviated from true fascist principles. In 1934, after falling out with Salazar, he was forced into exile in Belgium, where he continued his political writings. Upon returning to Portugal in 1941, he shifted his focus to promoting workers' rights and eventually served as a key advisor to President Américo Tomás, helping to implement significant labor reforms throughout the 1950s that modernized Portugal's industrial sector and strengthened trade unions.

Francisco Rolão Preto was a Portuguese political figure and journalist who founded the National Syndicalist Movement in 1932. He was one of the most prominent representatives of fascist ideology in Portugal during the early 20th century. Initially supporting António de Oliveira Salazar's Estado Novo regime, he later became disillusioned with Salazar's leadership and became a vocal opponent, leading to his exile in Spain in 1934. Preto's political philosophy combined traditional Catholic values with corporatist economic ideas and nationalist principles. After returning to Portugal in 1941, he continued his opposition to Salazar through his writings in various newspapers, eventually gaining support from the military establishment and helping to orchestrate the failed coup attempt of 1947, which led to his permanent exile in France where he lived until his death in 1962.

Francisco Rolão Preto was a prominent Portuguese politician and a key figure in the National Union, a conservative party in Portugal during the early 20th century. He served as the Minister of Public Works in the Estado Novo government from 1936 until 1939, implementing large-scale infrastructure projects to modernize the country's transportation systems. Rolão Preto also founded the Blue Shirts, Portugal's semi-official fascist militia, modeled closely after the Italian Fascist Party's paramilitary groups. Notably, his tenure as Minister was marked by the introduction of the New State's first five-year economic development plan, with an emphasis on agricultural growth and state-led investment in heavy industry.
